title: The Five Pillars of Islam
summary: The foundation on which the life of every Muslim is built.
body:
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Islam is built upon five."

1. Shahadah - the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger.
2. Salah - the five daily prayers: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.
3. Zakat - the obligatory annual charity of 2.5% on qualifying wealth held for a lunar year.
4. Sawm - fasting the month of Ramadan from Fajr to Maghrib.
5. Hajj - the pilgrimage to Makkah once in a lifetime for those who are able.

Each pillar is an act of worship that shapes character, discipline and gratitude.

title: The Six Pillars of Iman
summary: What a Muslim believes in the heart.
body:
Faith (iman) comprises belief in:

1. Allah - the One, unique, without partner or equal.
2. His angels - created from light, who carry out His commands.
3. His books - including the Qur’an, the final revelation preserved unchanged.
4. His messengers - from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ.
5. The Last Day - resurrection, reckoning and accountability.
6. Divine decree - the good and the bad, while a person still chooses and acts.

Belief is confirmed by the tongue and demonstrated through action.

title: How to Perform Wudu
body:
1. Intend purification and say Bismillah.
2. Wash both hands three times.
3. Rinse the mouth three times.
4. Sniff water into the nose and blow it out three times.
5. Wash the face three times, from forehead to chin, ear to ear.
6. Wash the arms to the elbows three times, right then left.
7. Wipe the head once with wet hands, then the ears.
8. Wash the feet to the ankles three times, right then left.

Wudu is broken by using the toilet, passing wind, and deep sleep. Water is not always needed: dry ablution (tayammum) is permitted when water is unavailable or harmful.

title: How to Pray Salah
summary: The steps of a complete unit of prayer.
body:
1. Face the Qibla and intend the specific prayer.
2. Say "Allahu Akbar" (takbir) to begin.
3. Recite Al-Fatihah, then a passage of the Qur’an.
4. Bow (ruku') saying "Subhana Rabbiyal-'Azim".
5. Rise saying "Sami'allahu liman hamidah", then "Rabbana wa lakal-hamd".
6. Prostrate (sujud) saying "Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la".
7. Sit between the two prostrations.
8. Prostrate a second time.

A rak'ah consists of these steps once. Fajr has 2 rak'at, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3 and Isha 4. The prayer closes with the tashahhud and tasleem.

RIFQ Muslim uses your GPS position to show prayer times and the Qibla direction for your exact location.

title: Understanding Zakat
summary: Who pays, on what, and how much.
body:
Zakat is due on wealth that reaches the nisab (the minimum threshold) and has been held for one lunar year.

The nisab is commonly measured as either 87.48 grams of gold or 612.36 grams of silver. Silver is often used because it is lower and therefore more inclusive.

The rate is 2.5% of qualifying wealth: cash, savings, gold and silver, trade goods and investments, plus money owed to you that you expect to be repaid. Debts you must pay are deducted.

Zakat is given to the eight categories named in the Qur’an (9:60), including the poor, the needy and those in debt. Use the Zakat calculator in this app with your local gold or silver price.

title: A Guide to Ramadan
summary: Fasting, suhoor, iftar and the last ten nights.
body:
Fasting begins at Fajr (suhoor ends) and ends at Maghrib (iftar). RIFQ Muslim computes both from your coordinates and timezone.

Sunnah of the day: wake for suhoor, delay it, break the fast promptly, and use the dua for breaking the fast.

Increase the Qur’an, charity and night prayer, especially in the last ten nights when Laylat al-Qadr is sought.

Those who are ill, travelling, pregnant, breastfeeding or menstruating have concessions; make up missed days or feed the needy as applicable.

Use the Ramadan screen for a 30-day timetable and the Tracker for daily worship.

title: The Hajj Journey
summary: The rites of pilgrimage in order.
body:
Hajj is performed in Dhul Hijjah:

1. Ihram - enter the sacred state with intention, before the miqat.
2. Tawaf - seven circuits of the Kaaba.
3. Sa'i - seven walks between Safa and Marwah.
4. 8th Dhul Hijjah - travel to Mina.
5. 9th - the day of Arafah, the essential rite, standing in supplication until sunset.
6. Muzdalifah - night under the open sky.
7. 10th - Jamarat (stoning), sacrifice, shaving or trimming, then Tawaf al-Ifadah.
8. 11th-12th - stone the three pillars after noon.
9. Tawaf al-Wada' - the farewell circuit before leaving.

Umrah is shorter: ihram, tawaf, sa'i, and trimming. See the Hajj guide screen for each step.

title: Daily Sunnah Checklist
body:
Morning and evening adhkar.
Pray the five prayers in their time, preferably in congregation.
Recite a portion of the Qur’an daily - even a page.
Sunnah and witr prayers.
Seek forgiveness 100 times a day.
Send salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ.
Give charity, even a little.
Maintain family ties.
Smile and speak kindly.
Sleep and wake with the sunnah duas.

Use the Worship tracker to keep these consistent; the Prophet ﷺ loved consistent deeds, even small ones.
